newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures slide but off lows.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures slide but off lows.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures extended their slide but managed to hold above day's lows by midsession on Thursday on scale-down industry buying, traders said.
Prices were due to open up to $200 down this morning after a wave of heavy selling in New York on Wednesday took September to eight-week low.
But London fared well above expectations, gapping just $85 lower and by the end of the morning dealing prices were just $35 to $65 easier.
September shed $50 at $1,815 per tonne while front-month July gave up $49 at $1,801. Volume reached a scant 1,491 lots.

Traders said London was also well underpinned due to general lack of selling. Origin sellers, particularly from Indonesia, were noticeably absent. This prompted talk that the Indonesian crop could be considerably lower than most had expected.
Some said Indonesian exporters were also struggling to cover their commitments and this could give rise to problems of contract defaults.
New York took a tumbled on forecasts of warmer temperature in Brazil's coffee belt. Technically, London could remain in a wide $1,770-$2,000 range basis September before the next decisive move.
